overview.text: The Pentagon is a large, five-sided government building in Arlington, Virginia, across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C. It serves as the headquarters of the U.S. military department, making it both a working center of military leadership and a widely recognized national symbol. The building was constructed during World War II as the federal government sought more room for the expanding War Department: work began on September 11, 1941, and the Pentagon officially opened on January 15, 1943. Its five-sided exterior and central courtyard are among the features recognized in its National Historic Landmark designation. Its location also reflects Arlington’s local history: construction displaced Queen City, an African American neighborhood, and other East Arlington residents.

key_facts.text: The Pentagon stands in Arlington, Virginia, across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C.
It is the headquarters of the U.S. military department.
Construction began September 11, 1941; the building officially opened January 15, 1943.
Its distinctive five-sided shape and central courtyard are among the features recognized in its 1992 National Historic Landmark designation.
The Pentagon project displaced Queen City, an African American community, and other East Arlington residents.
